title: Question file: data/<NN-slug>/questions.json
description: One file per chapter. Counts, word ranges and cross-field rules (number of correct options equals select, option count per type, keywords inside the stem, trap or misconception on wrong options) are checked by the question lint from SPEC.json, not here.

section.description: review link: '<file>#<section id>' inside the item's own chapter, for example '2-deep.md#a-shelf-belongs-to-one-region', or '<NN-slug>/<file>#<section id>' for a section of another chapter (required form for pool mock and drill). The section id is the heading anchor without the time box. Null only before the brief names a section.

services.description: in-scope service keys; services[0] is the focus service

exam_english.description: exam-English words that the stem uses on purpose; the word or one of its 'also' forms stands in the stem

concept.description: the one concept the question tests; with the traps it forms the coverage signature

qualifier.description: the capitalised qualifier phrase exactly as in the stem, for example 'LEAST operational overhead', or 'none'

keywords.description: deciding phrases, each copied exactly from the stem

explanation.description: why the key is right, with the mechanism; no option letters

twin.description: one line: the changed phrase and the answer it would lead to

sources.description: extra AWS pages beyond the evidence of the facts; usually empty

twin_of.description: set on the later question of a twin pair only; the earlier one has null

volatile.description: true when the key depends on a fact that changed in the volatile window

keyRev.description: raise when the set of correct options changes

authors.description: set by `q add`: the labels (--by) of every agent that wrote or replaced the question; none of them can be a solver of it

why.description: why this option is right, or which constraint or belief makes it wrong

misconception.description: the false belief in words, when no trap id fits

wrong_path.description: true when the think-aloud first follows a plausible wrong path: step 3 states the wrong prediction and step 5 holds the sentence that starts with questions.worked_wrong_path_marker

citations.description: sorted unique fact ids; a quote citation is stored as '<source_id>#<first 40 characters of the quote>'

citations_ok.description: open lens: every label had a citation and every citation verified

stem_only.description: closed lens: the solution stated before reading the options

case_option.description: ambiguity lens: the option id the solver argued for

edits.description: set by `q add --replace` in round 1: the one edit after a failed round is used
